tasks.title: HANGS Construction Services · FY2026 User Access Review
tasks.description: Test the IT general controls over HANGS Construction Services LLC’s accounting and payroll systems for the year ended June 30, 2026, from 12 Excel and Word files: the trial balance, the security and change policy, the HR roster and terminations, the June 30 user access report, the user listings of Ledgerwyn, Vellumrow, Charterfold and Quillpost, the sign-in settings, the change log, the payment releases and management’s answers. Match every account to a person, find leavers still active, conflicting duties and administrators, test the password and multi-factor settings and every change, and evaluate each deficiency. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks, management letter comments and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.

propertyEvents.result: Four systems in scope: Ledgerwyn, Vellumrow, Charterfold, Quillpost. The policy (approved by the board of directors on June 12, 2023) requires passwords of 12 characters, a lockout after 5 failed sign-ins, multi-factor sign-in for every account, leavers’ accounts disabled within 1 business day, a yearly access review, no shared accounts, administrator rights apart from transaction rights, 4 pairs of duties no one may hold together, and a ticket, a test and the CFO’s approval for every change. Materiality $340,000.00 (0.5% of $68,989,500.00 of revenue) is the yardstick for what a deficiency could let through.

propertyEvents.result: Classify each deficiency by what it could let through (AU-C 265, paraphrased)
propertyEvents.source: 07 Inquiries/IT general controls inquiries with management.docx
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; six inquiries about access and changes and the Controller’s written answers of August 5, 2026

propertyEvents.result: Proposed for the CPA. ITGC-03, the Controller’s unchecked administrator rights and the shared administrator, with $8,045,083.44 of entries no one reviewed and periods never locked: a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement would not be prevented or caught, a material weakness. ITGC-02 with ITGC-05: payments a person approves to vendors she set up, $64,675.50 so far, under a limit raised without approval; small against materiality but a fraud risk the board must hear of: a significant deficiency. ITGC-01, ITGC-04 and ITGC-06 (no access review since 2023, Q2): deficiencies, for the management letter. The CPA decides.

propertyEvents.result: Draft the management letter comments
propertyEvents.source: 07 Inquiries/IT general controls inquiries with management.docx
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; six inquiries about access and changes and the Controller’s written answers of August 5, 2026

propertyEvents.result: Six comments drafted, each with the condition, the policy it falls short of, the cause from management’s answers, the effect and a recommendation: disable leavers’ accounts on the last day across all four systems; take the AP Specialist’s approval right away and approve every vendor setup; separate the Controller’s administrator rights, retire the shared administrator, lock closed periods and turn on the approval step; enforce multi-factor sign-in everywhere; ticket, test and approve every change; review access every year. Management’s responses are blank for management to write.
